description: In the year to September 2026, gold, diamond and platinum jewellery cost 30.9% more across India and silver jewellery 87.8% more, while cars and jeeps cost 4.5% less and motorcycles and scooters 1.7% less (MoSPI's Consumer Price Index, provisional).

Gold jewellery rose over five times as much as consumer prices overall (5.5%). The 30.9% is MoSPI's price index for gold, diamond and platinum jewellery, not the price of gold itself. The map shows MoSPI's group 'Other personal effects' (jewellery and watches, with bags and the like) by state. These are all-India prices for September 2026 against September 2025, not festival-week prices. MoSPI cautions that state-level indices may rest on thin samples of price quotations. September's figures are provisional and will be revised with October's release on 12 November. Not advice to buy or sell anything.
question: What does your family buy at Dussehra?
x: In the year to September 2026: gold, diamond and platinum jewellery +30.9%, silver jewellery +87.8%, cars and jeeps −4.5%, two-wheelers −1.7%. Consumer prices overall +5.5%. Source: MoSPI CPI (base 2024), Sep 2026, provisional.
done: Every figure is read from MoSPI's all-India item table (read 15 Oct 2026 and re-read 16 Oct: all 637 rows match) and tested by the builder; the name of every item code is checked, and any figure typed into a card must be one the story reads from a table.

Numbers editor (independent) re-read the items and 23 states of each closing map live at MoSPI: no mismatch. Viewer editor: the hook, title and top bar now give the period and 'provisional', so the figures are not read as festival-week prices.
Our own finding is tested: gold jewellery's rise is 5.58 times the rise in consumer prices overall.
open: Listen to the narration end to end.
Post before 12 November, when October's index revises September.
